reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 the computer-name of the OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph must be a system-name: a COBOL word of at most 30 characters formed from A-Z (either case), 0-9 and hyphen (not first or last), not a reserved word of the 85 list (LENGTH, RANDOM and SUM included), and not one of this implementation's implementor-names or language-names, since the three types of system-name are disjoint; a literal or any other operand, and a clause written with no computer-name before it (85 nests the clauses inside the name's bracket), must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.Year < 2002 refuses (COBOL7624) a computer-name that is one of the implementation's implementor-names (the §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.2 disjointness); from 2002 the gate returns at once
the edition's reserved-word list: a word reserved only in a later edition (TYPEDEF, INTERFACE-ID) is free as a computer-name at 85; an 85 reserved word (FILE, SUM, RANDOM, LENGTH) is not
the COBOL word ceiling: 30 characters at 85, 63 at 2023 (COBOL1567)
Constructs.ComputerNameOptional2002: an OBJECT-COMPUTER clause (MEMORY SIZE, PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE) without a computer-name is refused before 2002 (COBOL0900)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 an implementor-name (C01, SWITCH-1, CONSOLE, DISK) is refused as a computer-name and accepted from 2002 (cn_feature printed RAN CNR8 at --std 2023); a clause with no computer-name before it is refused at 85 and legal from 2002; the reserved-word set and the word length differ by edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover implementor-names and later-edition reserved words as computer-names and the clauses in sequence; not exercised by them: feature- and switch-names, 85 reserved words including SUM, RANDOM and LENGTH, function-names, the character set, the 30-character limit, a clause with no computer-name (probed here).

reader.notes: System-name formation is implementor-defined within the character set (DOC-A.1-198: every well-formed system-name that is not an implementor-name is a computer-name); the 85 arm of GateComputerName reads the one ImplementorNameRegistry, and the reserved-word, length and character-set refusals come from the edition's word rules. Several refusals carry generic or §2023-cited diagnostics (COBOL0001, COBOL1970, COBOL3734), a wording matter only; every probe was accepted or refused as the text requires.
